--- title: "Household Location Burden Index" subtitle: "Analysis proposal — for review, only a base scenario exists so far" format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 2 embed-resources: true execute: echo: false warning: false message: false jupyter: july2025 --- **[← All run sets](../../index.qmd)** ::: {.callout-important} ## Status: proposal, one scenario registered Only a `base` scenario exists in this run set so far (the converged 2023 network, reused from the `v10.0-beta.2` study — no households added). No Control or Test scenario has been built or run, so the Burden Index itself cannot be computed yet. This page lays out the methodology, real baseline numbers from that one scenario, and the decisions needed before Control/Test scenarios get built. ::: ## The question > Maybe a combination approach could be useful? What if we calculated and > compared the additional Congested Roadway Capacity Demand (physical space > e.g. lane-mile minutes) from an extra 500 or 1000 typical households added > to specific locations around the region? We would use the TDM to estimate > the amount of peak-period roadway capacity added (which would include the > space-time footprint of the new households and their impact on delay for > others), based on the roadway travel that they would add to the system > (allowing for different modes to be chosen, and travel across the day for > various activities). > > This would be a measure of the burden placed on the system to access their > daily needs and opportunities, and it could be expressed as a percentage of > the burden placed by adding the extra HH to the geographic center of the > region which is in Murray. *"A household placed in Western Davis County > puts 1.6x more burden on the system"* — but if it's in one of Davis > County's identified City and Town Centers, it's only 1.2x as much burden. ## Proposed methodology **Design:** one converged **Base** run, one **Control** run (Base + N households added at a Murray TAZ — the geographic-center reference), and one **Test** run per candidate site (Base + the same N households added at that site's TAZ). Same household count everywhere, so differences reflect *location*, not household mix. ```{mermaid} flowchart LR SE[Base SE data] --> Base[Base run
no HH added] SE -->|+N HH at Murray| Control[Control run] SE -->|+N HH at Site A| SiteA[Test: Site A] SE -->|+N HH at Site B| SiteB[Test: Site B] SE -->|+N HH at Site …| SiteN[Test: Site …] Base --> Metric[ΔVHT = Test − Base
peak periods, congested V/C tiers] Control --> Metric SiteA --> Metric SiteB --> Metric SiteN --> Metric Metric --> Index["Burden Index(site) =
ΔVHT(site) / ΔVHT(Murray control)"] ``` **Metric:** systemwide congested vehicle-hours-traveled (ΔVHT), not just the new households' own trips — the whole point is capturing the delay imposed on *everyone else*, which only shows up as a regionwide before/after difference. Peak periods (AM, PM), filtered to links at or above a congestion threshold (V/C ≥ 0.8 and/or ≥ 1.0). **Burden Index** = ΔVHT(site) ÷ ΔVHT(Murray control) — giving the "1.6x" / "1.2x" style figure directly. ## Baseline signal, from the registered `base` scenario Real numbers, computed live from this run set's own committed data — not a pasted-in snapshot. `base` was registered via `import-manual-run`, reusing the already-converged `v10.0-beta.2-2023` raw network (same TDM ref) rather than spending Cube Voyager time re-running it from scratch; no households have been added to it. The table below aggregates its curated segment-level summary directly, applying the same V/C≥0.8 / V/C≥1.0 tiering `02_Summarize_HighwayNet.s` would. ::: {#baseline-table .cell execution_count=2} | Period | Total VHT | VHT at V/C ≥ 0.8 | VHT at V/C ≥ 1.0 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | AM | 225,355 | 66,522 (29.5%) | 17,225 (7.6%) | | MD | 405,888 | 43,243 (10.7%) | 908 (0.2%) | | PM | 338,003 | 146,780 (43.4%) | 51,135 (15.1%) | | EV | 312,990 | 115 (0.0%) | 0 (0.0%) | Regionwide lane-miles in this network: **9,014** (segment-direction rows). ::: This is *system scale*, not the site-comparison metric itself — it's today's regionwide congested-VHT backdrop that a 500–1000-household ΔVHT would be measured against. PM is the most congested period by a wide margin; AM is a distant second; MD and EV carry almost no V/C≥1.0 congestion. This confirms AM+PM is the right peak-period scope for the Burden Index, and suggests PM alone may show the clearest site-to-site differences. ::: {.callout-note} ## What's still missing for Control/Test scenarios This `base` scenario only has the segment summary curated so far — the regionwide *congestion-tier* summary (`Summary_HighwayNet.csv`, needed for the Δ calculation once Control/Test scenarios exist) requires the custom driver-script edit described below, then re-registering `base` with that output included too. Adding Control/Test scenarios still needs real Cube Voyager runs — see "Decisions needed" and "Effort and runtime" below. ::: ## What the model already gives us to work with This isn't hypothetical — the pieces exist in the TDM today, just not wired together for this purpose: | Need | Existing TDM piece | Status | |---|---|---| | Systemwide VMT/VHT by period, purpose, and congestion tier (V/C ≥ 0.8, ≥ 1.0) | `2_ModelScripts/7_PostProcessing/4_BCA_Summaries/02_Summarize_HighwayNet.s` | Exists, does exactly this — but its `READ FILE` line is **commented out** in the default driver script, so it doesn't currently run | | A way to add households to a specific TAZ without touching anything else | `WFRC_SEFile` / `MAG_SEFile` — plain TAZ-level `TOTHH`/`HHPOP` CSVs | Exists; this framework already has a proven pattern for generating per-scenario SE variants (used for the `non-motorized-2023` study) | | A converged 2023 base network to build on | The `v10.0-beta.2` run set's `Base_2023` scenario, already run in this repo | **Done** — registered as this run set's own `base` scenario via `import-manual-run`, no re-run needed | | Household composition (size, income, workers, autos) for the "typical household" | `1_HHDisag_AutoOwn/` (LifeCycle → HHDisaggregation → AutoOwnership) | The model derives this itself from `TOTHH`/`HHPOP`, using distributions that already respond to local accessibility — there's no separate lever to force a specific household profile | | Tighter convergence / warm-start across runs, to keep a 500–1000 HH signal from being swamped by run-to-run noise | — | **Not found.** No iteration-count, RMSE, or warm-start key is exposed in the Control Center. This needs an answer from whoever maintains the TDM's feedback-loop scripts before results can be trusted at this small a scale | ## How this fits the run-management framework Mechanically, this is a new run set — `household-location-burden` — following the same pattern already proven by `non-motorized-2023` and `bring-work-trips-closer-to-home`: - **`base`** scenario — **done**. Registered by reusing the existing converged `v10.0-beta.2-2023` run rather than re-running full feedback from scratch. To pick up the BCA congestion-tier summary once the driver script is edited, its raw folder can be re-entered via `start_at_label` (resuming just the post-processing steps) rather than a full re-run. - **`control-murray`** and one **`site-`** scenario per candidate location — each pointed at its own generated SE file via `overrides.WFRC_SEFile`, the same relative-path mechanism `non-motorized-2023` uses. - A shared **custom driver script** (this run set's own copy of `__HailMary_1Subfolder.s`, with the BCA summary line turned on) — the framework's existing `driver_script` mechanism, no core code changes needed. - **Outputs curated**: just the small `Summary_HighwayNet.csv` per scenario — well under the size ceiling, no raw network/matrix files committed. - A small Burden Index calculation module, reported here once real runs exist — same shape as `non-motorized-2023`'s `report_loader.py`. No changes to the TDM codebase, the orchestrator's core logic, or how Cube Voyager runs are required — this is entirely new configuration plus one custom driver script, the same category of work as every other run set in this repo. ## Decisions needed before building this | Decision | Options | Recommendation | If left unresolved | |---|---|---|---| | **N** — households per site | 500 or 1000 | 1000, for a stronger signal against regional noise (see convergence risk below) | Defaults to 500 (boss's first-mentioned number) | | **Congestion threshold** | V/C ≥ 0.8, ≥ 1.0, or report both | Report both — cheap, since both are already in the same summary CSV | Defaults to reporting both | | **Peak window** | AM+PM only, or all four periods | AM+PM, matching "peak-period" in the original ask; MD/EV available in the same file if wanted later | Defaults to AM+PM | | **Site list** | Western Davis County, Davis County's designated City/Town Centers (Wasatch Choice RCP centers), plus other target geographies | Needs a real TAZ list. No City/Town Centers layer was found in this repo's TDM inputs — likely needs to come from WFRC's regional centers GIS layer | **Blocks starting the build** — this is the one open item that isn't just a config default | | **Convergence / noise mitigation** | (a) increase feedback iterations for these runs specifically, (b) run each site multiple times and average, (c) accept single-run noise and caveat results | Needs input from whoever maintains the TDM's feedback-loop scripts — no Control Center lever was found for this | Results could be dominated by run-to-run noise rather than the effect being measured | ## Effort and runtime Each Test/Control scenario needs a **full feedback run** (mode choice logsums + four-period assignment) — households are added before disaggregation, so nothing upstream can be skipped or reused between sites. Only the Base run benefits from reuse. Runtime scales linearly with number of sites; `max_parallel_runs` (already supported, not yet exercised on a real multi-scenario batch) could help once Cube Voyager licensing/hardware limits on this workstation are confirmed. Suggested build order: 1. Confirm the Base-run reuse strategy and the driver-script edit; validate `Summary_HighwayNet.csv` comes out as expected on the existing Base run alone. 2. Build SE generation + one real site + the Murray control; validate the ΔVHT / Burden Index math end-to-end on real output before committing to the full site list. 3. Once proven, add the remaining sites from the confirmed list. ## Bottom line The metric, the SE-modification mechanism, and the run-set framework are all already proven in this repo for other studies — this is a matter of configuration and one small driver-script change, not new engineering. What's missing before this can start is **the site list** and **a convergence strategy**; both need a decision from outside this repo before any model time is spent.
